title: Relief from a No-Show Penalty where the Airline Has Moved the Schedule
content:
An airline that has moved the schedule of an Air Ticket Fare Brands booking may relieve the booking of part or all of the penalty otherwise withheld for a no-show. Relief turns on the largest single schedule move the airline has advised on the booking, measured against the schedule-change threshold of the fare brand held, together with the receipt of a recent notice.

## 1. The ladder

| Where | The share withheld is |
| --- | --- |
| the largest single schedule move advised on the booking reaches the brand's schedule-change threshold, and at least 1 such notice was received in the last 3 months | 0, so that no part of the penalty is withheld |
| the largest single schedule move advised on the booking, multiplied by 2, reaches the brand's threshold while the move itself does not, and at least 1 such notice was received in the last 3 months | 0.5, being 50 percent, so that half of the penalty is withheld |
| in every other case | no such relief is given |

The window for the notice count is 3 months, counted back from today over the schedule-change notices standing on the booking. The move that decides the first two rows is the largest single one advised, not the sum of several.

## 2. The brand thresholds the ladder is read against

| Fare brand | Schedule-change threshold (minutes) |
| --- | --- |
| Basic Economy Lite | 180 |
| Economy Saver | 180 |
| Economy Classic | 120 |
| Economy Flex | 120 |
| Premium Economy Select | 90 |
| Business Saver | 60 |
| Business Flex | 60 |

## 3. Boundary readings, on hypothetical figures

On a Premium Economy Select booking, whose threshold stands at 90 minutes: a largest move of 90 minutes reaches the threshold exactly, so with a notice inside the last 3 months the share withheld is 0. A largest move of 50 minutes does not reach 90, but 50 multiplied by 2 is 100, which does, so with such a notice the share withheld is 0.5. A largest move of 40 minutes reaches neither test, since 40 multiplied by 2 is 80 and falls short of 90, so no such relief is given.

On the same booking a largest move of 120 minutes with the most recent notice standing 5 months back meets neither row, because both turn on a notice received inside the last 3 months.
